composing_text: 71st Infantry Brigade; 158th Infantry Brigade; 160th Infantry Brigade
notes: Arrival in Normandy 27 June per Wikipedia list (landing beach not given). Fighting in July.

current_activity: Preliminary attacks: captures Cahier and holds it with difficulty against heavy counter-attacks
notes: Event date: 15-17 July 1944 (night of the 15th to the 17th) (Ellis, vol. I, p. 334). Event definition: In the fighting before Goodwood the division, on the right of the 15th Division in XII Corps, captures Cahier, is heavily counter-attacked and only with difficulty keeps its gain. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 334: "On their right 53rd Division captured Cahier but were heavily counter-attacked and only with difficulty maintained their gain". Location: Evrecy, Calvados (new place), standing for the Cahier area on the Evrecy road with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Evrecy, the town on the road whose approaches include Cahier; Cahier itself is not located. Location support: Ellis names Cahier but the hamlet is not in the gazetteers used; the Evrecy road it lies on is named in the same paragraph (p. 334).

current_activity: Follows the German withdrawal: by nightfall has cleared the east bank of the Orne almost as far as Grimbosq
notes: Event date: 5 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 408). Event definition: On 5 August, meeting fewer mines and only weak infantry detachments, the division on the left of XII Corps clears the east bank of the Orne almost as far as Grimbosq by nightfall (p. 408). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 408: "By nightfall the 53rd Division (on the left) had cleared the east bank of the Orne almost as far as Grimbos". Location: Grimbosq, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Grimbosq, the limit of the advance; the page says almost as far as it. Location support: Ellis names Grimbosq as the limit of the clearing of the east bank (p. 408).

current_activity: Pheasant: takes 's-Hertogenbosch after house-to-house fighting; resistance ceases and the garrison commander surrenders
notes: Event date: 27 October 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 124). Event definition: The division gains a first footing in 's-Hertogenbosch by hard fighting early on 24 October and then spends two days in house-to-house fighting and in bridging the network of waterways to capture the old fortress town; a small counter-attack on the western outskirts is beaten off on the 27th, when resistance ceases and the garrison commander surrenders (p. 124). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 124: "but the 53rd Division by hard fighting gained a first footing in s'Hertogenbosch early on the 24th"; "Two days were occupied by the 53rd Division in house-to-house fighting to capture the old fortress town of s'Hertogenbosch"; "when resistance ceased and the garrison commander surrendered". Location: 's-Hertogenbosch, Noord-Brabant (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of 's-Hertogenbosch; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names 's-Hertogenbosch as the town the division captured (p. 124). Context: Flagged addition: a 1944 row added in British Batch 2 only so that the new OP-PHEASANT has a British claim (Wikipedia, R672, for the name and dates).

current_activity: Ardennes: with the 33rd Armoured Brigade clears the area south-east of Marche and takes Grimbiemont; relieved on the 8th
notes: Event date: 3 January 1945 (the capture of Grimbiemont is before the relief on the 8th; the day is not given) (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 190, 191). Event definition: In the XXX Corps attack that begins on 3 January, on the left, the division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade, despite enemy counter-attacks, clear the area south-east from Marche and capture Grimbiemont, where they are relieved on the 8th by the 51st Division; the page does not give the day of the capture of Grimbiemont (pp. 190-191). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, pp. 190-191: "On the left the 53rd Division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade, despite enemy counter-attacks, cleared the area south-east from Marche and captured Grimbiemont, where they were relieved on the 8th by the 51st Division". Location: Marche-en-Famenne, Luxembourg (existing place PL0210), the town from which the area was cleared south-eastwards with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Marche-en-Famenne; Grimbiemont, the place named, is a hamlet some miles to the south-east and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Marche as the point from which the division cleared the area south-east (p. 190).
